title: This Nightmare Situation Is Why You Need To Be Careful With Extended Warranties!
summary: A repair shop recounts a transmission claim Endurance denied by citing a trivial, pre-existing tire-size mismatch.

assertions.quote: trying to find a way to not pay it

verdicts.note: Widely reported complaint pattern (tire-size, maintenance-record technicalities), though not universal; reputable providers do pay valid claims.

assertions.quote: if you modify it and you modify something, it's not a factor anymore

verdicts.note: Contracts commonly exclude modification-related failures, but providers have also been reported stretching this to deny unrelated claims.

FTC says using aftermarket/recycled parts keeps a warranty in effect unless the part itself caused the damage, in which case the manufacturer/dealer can deny coverage for the damaged part -- so modification only voids coverage when it actually causes the failure, not automatically.

assertions.quote: the adjuster will be out, you know, within the next 24 hours

verdicts.note: Consistent with widely reported complaints about slow inspection scheduling and claims processing.
A standard, documented requirement across most vehicle service contracts.
FTC confirms a warranty company could ask for maintenance records and that a claim "might be denied" without them, but doesn't speak to whether the request itself delays the repair.
